title.en: Pregnant in Tennessee? TennCare + Coverage Options 2026
title.es: Embarazada en Tennessee? TennCare y Opciones 2026

description.en: Pregnant in Tennessee in 2026? TennCare covers prenatal care through 250% FPL ($54,100 for a household of 2). Compare TennCare, CoverKids, and ACA options.
description.es: Embarazada en Tennessee en 2026? TennCare cubre atencion prenatal hasta el 250% del FPL ($54,100 para un hogar de 2). Compare TennCare, CoverKids y ACA.

h1.en: Pregnant in Tennessee in 2026? Here Are Your Coverage Options
h1.es: Embarazada en Tennessee en 2026? Aqui Estan Sus Opciones de Cobertura

subhero.en: TennCare covers pregnant Tennessee women earning up to 250% FPL ($54,100/year for a household of 2). Apply year-round through TennCare Connect with no enrollment deadline. Coverage includes prenatal care, delivery, and 12 months of postpartum care.
subhero.es: TennCare cubre a mujeres embarazadas de Tennessee que ganan hasta el 250% del FPL ($54,100/ano para un hogar de 2). Solicite durante todo el ano sin fecha limite a traves de TennCare Connect.

heading.en: TennCare pregnancy coverage is year-round with no deadline
heading.es: La cobertura de embarazo de TennCare esta disponible todo el ano sin fecha limite

body.en: Tennessee's TennCare program accepts pregnancy applications at any point during pregnancy, with no enrollment period or open enrollment deadline. Coverage starts from the date of your application approval and can be retroactive up to 3 months in some cases. Apply as early in your pregnancy as possible to ensure prenatal care is covered from the start.
body.es: El programa TennCare de Tennessee acepta solicitudes de embarazo en cualquier momento durante el embarazo, sin periodo de inscripcion ni fecha limite. La cobertura comienza desde la fecha de aprobacion de su solicitud y puede ser retroactiva hasta 3 meses en algunos casos.

label.en: ACA Marketplace SEP (if you lose pregnancy-related coverage)
label.es: SEP del Mercado ACA (si pierde cobertura relacionada con el embarazo)

quickAnswer.en: Pregnant women in Tennessee can apply for TennCare year-round if household income is at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Level ($54,100/year for a pregnant woman counted as a household of 2 in 2026). TennCare covers all prenatal visits, ultrasounds, labor and delivery, and 12 months of postpartum care at no cost. Tennessee has not expanded Medicaid under the ACA, so non-pregnant adults with low income may face a coverage gap, but pregnant women get generous income limits regardless of expansion status. If income exceeds the TennCare limit, ACA Marketplace plans through healthcare.gov offer subsidized coverage, and CoverKids (Tennessee's CHIP program) covers children up to 250% FPL after birth.
quickAnswer.es: Las mujeres embarazadas en Tennessee pueden solicitar TennCare durante todo el ano si el ingreso del hogar es igual o inferior al 250% del Nivel de Pobreza Federal ($54,100/ano para una mujer embarazada contada como hogar de 2 en 2026). TennCare cubre todas las visitas prenatales, ultrasonidos, parto y 12 meses de atencion postparto sin costo. Si el ingreso supera el limite de TennCare, los planes del Mercado ACA a traves de healthcare.gov ofrecen cobertura subsidiada.

introParagraphs.en: Pregnancy in Tennessee opens one of the most generous Medicaid pathways in the state. TennCare, Tennessee's Medicaid program, covers pregnant women with household incomes up to 250% of the Federal Poverty Level regardless of immigration status considerations and without the usual non-expansion-state restrictions that leave other low-income adults without coverage. For 2026, that income limit is $54,100 per year for a pregnant woman (who is counted as a household of 2, herself and her unborn child), $68,300 for a household of 3, or $82,500 for a household of 4. Coverage includes every medically necessary prenatal service: office visits, labs, ultrasounds, mental health care, substance use treatment, and hospitalization for labor and delivery. Critically, TennCare now provides 12 full months of postpartum coverage after delivery, a major expansion from the prior 60-day limit. There is no open enrollment window; apply any time during pregnancy through TennCare Connect at tenncareconnect.tn.gov or by calling 1-855-259-0701.
introParagraphs.es: El embarazo en Tennessee abre uno de los accesos mas generosos a Medicaid en el estado. TennCare, el programa Medicaid de Tennessee, cubre a mujeres embarazadas con ingresos del hogar hasta el 250% del Nivel de Pobreza Federal sin las restricciones habituales de los estados sin expansion que dejan a otros adultos de bajos ingresos sin cobertura. Para 2026, ese limite de ingresos es $54,100 por ano para una mujer embarazada (contada como hogar de 2), $68,300 para un hogar de 3, o $82,500 para un hogar de 4. La cobertura incluye todos los servicios prenatales medicamente necesarios: visitas de consultorio, laboratorios, ultrasonidos, atencion de salud mental, tratamiento de uso de sustancias y hospitalizacion para el parto. TennCare ahora proporciona 12 meses completos de cobertura postparto despues del parto.

introParagraphs.en: Tennessee's coverage landscape during pregnancy has two critical gaps to understand. First, Tennessee has not expanded Medicaid under the ACA, so non-pregnant adults without dependent children who earn above 100% FPL ($15,960 single in 2026) but below the ACA subsidy floor face a coverage gap where TennCare is unavailable and Marketplace premium tax credits do not apply. Pregnancy removes a woman from this gap entirely during the pregnancy period and for 12 months postpartum. Second, the ACA subsidy cliff returned January 1, 2026 (enhanced premium tax credits from the American Rescue Plan Act and Inflation Reduction Act expired), which means pregnant women who earn above 250% FPL and use the Marketplace must now pay more than they did in 2024 and 2025. Women in this income range should compare TennCare (if they qualify) against ACA Silver plans with cost-sharing reductions at 100% to 250% FPL, which remain the most valuable Marketplace option below the 400% FPL cliff at $86,560 for a household of 2 in 2026. For questions about what Medicaid covers during pregnancy, including mental health and substance use services, see the Medicaid income limits reference and the ACA income limits guide for Tennessee residents above the TennCare threshold.
introParagraphs.es: El panorama de cobertura en Tennessee durante el embarazo tiene dos brechas criticas que comprender. Tennessee no ha expandido Medicaid bajo la ACA, por lo que los adultos no embarazados sin hijos dependientes que ganan por encima del 100% del FPL pero por debajo del umbral de subsidios del Mercado enfrentan una brecha de cobertura. El embarazo elimina a una mujer de esta brecha completamente durante el periodo de embarazo y por 12 meses postparto. Ademas, el acantilado de subsidios ACA regreso el 1 de enero de 2026 (los creditos fiscales de primas mejorados expiraron), lo que significa que las mujeres embarazadas que ganan mas del 250% del FPL y usan el Mercado deben pagar mas que en 2024 y 2025.

name.en: Check your income against the TennCare pregnancy threshold
name.es: Verifique su ingreso en comparacion con el umbral de embarazo de TennCare

text.en: TennCare counts a pregnant woman as a household of 2 (herself and her unborn child). For 2026, the income limit is 250% FPL: $54,100/year if you live alone, $68,300 for a household of 3 (you, partner, and unborn child), $82,500 for a household of 4. Use your current monthly income, not last year's tax return. If you are within range, apply immediately through TennCare Connect at tenncareconnect.tn.gov.
text.es: TennCare cuenta a una mujer embarazada como un hogar de 2 (ella y su hijo por nacer). Para 2026, el limite de ingresos es el 250% del FPL: $54,100/ano si vive sola, $68,300 para un hogar de 3, $82,500 para un hogar de 4. Use su ingreso mensual actual, no su declaracion de impuestos del ano pasado.

name.en: Apply through TennCare Connect (year-round, no deadline)
name.es: Solicite a traves de TennCare Connect (durante todo el ano, sin fecha limite)

text.en: Submit your TennCare application at tenncareconnect.tn.gov or call 1-855-259-0701. You can also apply in person at a Tennessee Department of Human Services (DHS) office or through a certified application assister. Tennessee processes pregnancy applications on a priority basis; coverage can begin the month you apply and, in some cases, be retroactive up to 3 months if you received prenatal services before your application was processed. Bring proof of pregnancy (doctor's statement or positive pregnancy test with estimated due date) to speed processing.
text.es: Envie su solicitud de TennCare en tenncareconnect.tn.gov o llame al 1-855-259-0701. Tambien puede solicitar en persona en una oficina del Departamento de Servicios Humanos (DHS) de Tennessee. La cobertura puede comenzar el mes en que solicita y, en algunos casos, ser retroactiva hasta 3 meses.

name.en: Gather and submit your required documents
name.es: Recopile y envie sus documentos requeridos

text.en: Upload to TennCare Connect or bring to a DHS office: proof of pregnancy (physician letter or positive test result showing estimated due date), proof of Tennessee residency (utility bill, lease, or Tennessee ID), proof of income (most recent pay stubs or employer letter if self-employed), Social Security number or documentation of immigration status for each household member, and photo identification. Incomplete applications cause processing delays; submit all documents at once when possible.
text.es: Suba a TennCare Connect o lleve a una oficina de DHS: prueba de embarazo (carta medica o resultado positivo de prueba con fecha estimada de parto), prueba de residencia en Tennessee, prueba de ingresos (talones de pago recientes), numero de Seguro Social o documentacion de estado migratorio para cada miembro del hogar, y identificacion con foto.

name.en: Enroll your newborn in TennCare or CoverKids immediately after birth
name.es: Inscriba a su recien nacido en TennCare o CoverKids inmediatamente despues del nacimiento

text.en: If you are enrolled in TennCare when your baby is born, your newborn is automatically deemed eligible for TennCare for the first year of life with no separate application required. Report the birth to TennCare Connect within 10 days to activate your baby's coverage. If your income exceeds TennCare's postpartum limit, apply your newborn to CoverKids (Tennessee's CHIP program) at tenncareconnect.tn.gov; CoverKids covers children up to 250% FPL ($54,100 for a household of 2) at no or low cost.
text.es: Si esta inscrita en TennCare cuando nace su bebe, su recien nacido se considera automaticamente elegible para TennCare durante el primer ano de vida sin necesidad de una solicitud separada. Informe el nacimiento a TennCare Connect dentro de los 10 dias para activar la cobertura de su bebe. Si su ingreso supera el limite postparto de TennCare, solicite CoverKids para su recien nacido en tenncareconnect.tn.gov.

name.en: Confirm your postpartum TennCare coverage extends 12 months after delivery
name.es: Confirme que su cobertura postparto de TennCare se extiende 12 meses despues del parto

text.en: Tennessee extended postpartum TennCare coverage to a full 12 months after delivery, up from the prior 60-day limit. After your baby is born, contact TennCare Connect to confirm your postpartum coverage is active and review what services are covered, including postpartum depression screening, family planning, chronic condition management, and well-woman visits. Coverage ends at 12 months postpartum unless you qualify for TennCare under another eligibility category such as parental TennCare (parents at 100% FPL or below for 2026).
text.es: Tennessee extendio la cobertura postparto de TennCare a 12 meses completos despues del parto. Despues de que nazca su bebe, contacte a TennCare Connect para confirmar que su cobertura postparto esta activa y revisar que servicios estan cubiertos, incluyendo deteccion de depresion postparto, planificacion familiar y visitas de bienestar para la mujer.

name.en: If income exceeds TennCare limits, compare ACA Marketplace plans through healthcare.gov
name.es: Si el ingreso supera los limites de TennCare, compare planes del Mercado ACA a traves de healthcare.gov

text.en: Pregnant women in Tennessee with income above 250% FPL ($54,100 for household of 2) can enroll in ACA Marketplace plans at healthcare.gov during Open Enrollment (November 1, 2026 to January 15, 2027 for the 2027 plan year) or during a Special Enrollment Period triggered by a qualifying life event. Pregnancy itself is not a standalone SEP trigger; however, if you recently lost other coverage, moved to Tennessee, or experienced another qualifying event, you have a 60-day Marketplace SEP. ACA plans must cover maternity care, prenatal visits, and labor and delivery as essential health benefits. Silver plans at 100% to 250% FPL include cost-sharing reductions that significantly lower deductibles and copays.
text.es: Las mujeres embarazadas en Tennessee con ingresos superiores al 250% del FPL ($54,100 para hogar de 2) pueden inscribirse en planes del Mercado ACA en healthcare.gov durante la Inscripcion Abierta o durante un Periodo de Inscripcion Especial. Los planes ACA deben cubrir atencion de maternidad, visitas prenatales y parto como beneficios esenciales de salud.

name.en: Update your Marketplace subsidy when household size changes after birth
name.es: Actualice su subsidio del Mercado cuando cambie el tamano del hogar despues del nacimiento

text.en: Birth is a qualifying life event that triggers a 60-day Marketplace Special Enrollment Period. Log in to healthcare.gov and report the birth to update your household size. Adding your newborn increases household size by one, which lowers your income as a percentage of FPL and typically increases your premium tax credit. For example, a single woman at $60,000 moves from 277% FPL (household-of-1) to 220% FPL (household-of-2) after her baby is born, potentially qualifying for a lower Silver plan premium. Submit the updated enrollment within 60 days of the birth date.
text.es: El nacimiento es un evento calificado de vida que activa un Periodo de Inscripcion Especial de 60 dias en el Mercado. Inicie sesion en healthcare.gov e informe el nacimiento para actualizar el tamano de su hogar. Agregar a su recien nacido aumenta el tamano del hogar en uno, lo que reduce su ingreso como porcentaje del FPL y tipicamente aumenta su credito fiscal de primas.

stateRules.rule: TennCare covers pregnant women at 250% FPL ($54,100/year for a household of 2 counting pregnant woman + unborn child, 2026). Coverage includes all medically necessary prenatal services, labor, delivery, and 12 months of postpartum care. Tennessee is not a Medicaid expansion state; non-pregnant adults without dependent children face a coverage gap at incomes between 0% and 100% FPL. Parents and caretakers qualify for TennCare at up to 105% FPL ($16,758 for a single parent in 2026, reflecting the 100% FPL standard with the 5% income disregard applied).

CoverKids (Tennessee's CHIP program) covers children ages 0-18 with household incomes at or below 250% FPL. Newborns born to TennCare-enrolled mothers are automatically deemed eligible for TennCare for the first year of life. Apply through TennCare Connect at tenncareconnect.tn.gov.

Tennessee extended postpartum TennCare coverage to 12 full months after delivery. Postpartum coverage includes postpartum depression screening, family planning services, chronic condition management, and well-woman visits. After 12 months, a separate eligibility review determines if the mother qualifies under parental TennCare (100% FPL) or another category.

en: Income above 250% FPL when calculated correctly: TennCare counts the pregnant woman and unborn child as a household of 2; failing to include the unborn child inflates the FPL percentage and may incorrectly suggest ineligibility
Missing or insufficient proof of pregnancy: a home pregnancy test photo is not accepted; TennCare requires a physician letter, clinical records, or formal prenatal visit documentation
Not a Tennessee resident: applicants must provide proof of current Tennessee residency; an out-of-state address at the time of application triggers denial

Immigration status documentation gap: qualified immigrants are eligible for TennCare pregnancy coverage, but documentation must be submitted with the application; undocumented immigrants can access emergency delivery coverage only through the Emergency Medicaid pathway

Reporting incorrect household composition: household size for TennCare pregnancy calculations includes all family members living together, not just the pregnant woman; under-reporting or over-reporting household members changes the FPL calculation
es: Ingreso superior al 250% del FPL cuando se calcula correctamente: TennCare cuenta a la mujer embarazada y al hijo por nacer como un hogar de 2; no incluir al hijo por nacer infla el porcentaje del FPL y puede sugerir incorrectamente la inelegibilidad
Prueba de embarazo faltante o insuficiente: una foto de una prueba de embarazo casera no es aceptada; TennCare requiere una carta medica, registros clinicos o documentacion formal de visita prenatal
No ser residente de Tennessee: los solicitantes deben proporcionar prueba de residencia actual en Tennessee; una direccion fuera del estado al momento de la solicitud desencadena una denegacion

Brecha de documentacion de estado migratorio: los inmigrantes calificados son elegibles para la cobertura de embarazo de TennCare, pero la documentacion debe enviarse con la solicitud; los inmigrantes no documentados solo pueden acceder a la cobertura de parto de emergencia a traves de la via de Medicaid de Emergencia

Reporte incorrecto de la composicion del hogar: el tamano del hogar para los calculos de embarazo de TennCare incluye a todos los miembros de la familia que viven juntos, no solo a la mujer embarazada

heading.en: TennCare vs Marketplace vs Employer Plan: Which Is Best During Pregnancy in Tennessee?
heading.es: TennCare vs Mercado vs Plan del Empleador: Cual es Mejor Durante el Embarazo en Tennessee?

body.en: TennCare is the default first choice for pregnant women in Tennessee whose income falls at or below 250% FPL ($54,100 for a household of 2 in 2026). TennCare covers prenatal care, delivery, and 12 months postpartum at zero cost to the enrollee, which makes it the strongest financial value for any qualifying pregnant woman regardless of immigration status for qualified immigrants. ACA Marketplace plans are the alternative for income above 250% FPL, but require awareness of two 2026 realities: the ACA subsidy cliff returned January 1, 2026 (enhanced PTCs expired), and pregnancy does not itself trigger a Marketplace SEP. Women above the TennCare income limit who do not have a qualifying event for a Marketplace SEP must rely on an existing employer plan or wait for the next Open Enrollment period (November 1, 2026). Employer plans are required to cover maternity care as an essential health benefit under the ACA, with typical additional monthly costs of $200 to $500 for adding dependent maternity coverage. COBRA is rarely the right choice during pregnancy: at 102% of the full employer and employee premium combined, COBRA typically runs $700 to $2,200 per month and is only worth considering for a pregnant woman who has a specific specialist providing ongoing high-risk obstetric care that is not in any Marketplace or TennCare network. The decision matrix for Tennessee pregnant women is: TennCare first (income at or below 250% FPL, year-round, free); then employer plan if available and income exceeds TennCare limits; then Marketplace with subsidies for income between 250% and 400% FPL if a qualifying event exists; COBRA as last resort only.
body.es: TennCare es la primera opcion predeterminada para las mujeres embarazadas en Tennessee cuyo ingreso es igual o inferior al 250% del FPL ($54,100 para un hogar de 2 en 2026). TennCare cubre atencion prenatal, parto y 12 meses postparto sin costo para el inscrito. Los planes del Mercado ACA son la alternativa para ingresos superiores al 250% del FPL, pero requieren conocer dos realidades de 2026: el acantilado de subsidios ACA regreso el 1 de enero de 2026, y el embarazo en si mismo no activa un SEP del Mercado. COBRA rara vez es la opcion correcta durante el embarazo: al 102% de la prima completa, COBRA tipicamente cuesta entre $700 y $2,200 al mes.

intro.en: The most costly mistakes pregnant Tennessee women make when seeking coverage in 2026:
intro.es: Los errores mas costosos que cometen las mujeres embarazadas de Tennessee al buscar cobertura en 2026:

items.en: Not applying for TennCare because they assume Tennessee's non-expansion status means they are ineligible. Tennessee has not expanded Medicaid for most adults, but pregnant women qualify at the generous 250% FPL threshold regardless of expansion status. This is one of the most misunderstood distinctions in Tennessee's coverage landscape.
items.es: No solicitar TennCare porque asumen que el estatus de no expansion de Tennessee significa que no son elegibles. Tennessee no ha expandido Medicaid para la mayoria de los adultos, pero las mujeres embarazadas califican al generoso umbral del 250% del FPL independientemente del estatus de expansion.

items.en: Calculating household size without counting the unborn child. TennCare counts a pregnant woman and her unborn child as a household of 2. A pregnant woman living alone should compare her income to the household-of-2 limit ($54,100 in 2026), not the household-of-1 limit ($39,900). This single error causes many eligible women to incorrectly conclude they do not qualify.
items.es: Calcular el tamano del hogar sin contar al hijo por nacer. TennCare cuenta a una mujer embarazada y a su hijo por nacer como un hogar de 2. Una mujer embarazada que vive sola debe comparar su ingreso con el limite del hogar de 2 ($54,100 en 2026), no con el limite del hogar de 1 ($39,900).

items.en: Assuming COBRA is the safest choice during pregnancy because it continues the same plan. COBRA runs 102% of the full combined employer and employee premium, often $1,000 to $2,500 per month for a family plan. TennCare provides equivalent or superior prenatal coverage at zero cost for qualifying incomes. Compare TennCare eligibility first before electing COBRA.
items.es: Asumir que COBRA es la opcion mas segura durante el embarazo porque continua el mismo plan. COBRA cuesta el 102% de la prima completa combinada del empleador y el empleado, a menudo entre $1,000 y $2,500 al mes para un plan familiar. TennCare proporciona cobertura prenatal equivalente o superior sin costo para ingresos calificados.

items.en: Missing the newborn enrollment window. Even though TennCare-enrolled mothers get automatic deemed coverage for their newborn, Marketplace-enrolled mothers must actively add the newborn to their Marketplace plan within 60 days of birth or through CoverKids at TennCare Connect. Failing to report the birth by day 60 leaves the newborn uncovered until the next Open Enrollment.
items.es: Perder la ventana de inscripcion del recien nacido. Aunque las madres inscritas en TennCare obtienen cobertura automatica para su recien nacido, las madres inscritas en el Mercado deben agregar activamente al recien nacido a su plan del Mercado dentro de los 60 dias del nacimiento o a traves de CoverKids en TennCare Connect.

items.en: Stopping TennCare coverage immediately after delivery and not utilizing the 12-month postpartum benefit. Tennessee's 12-month postpartum TennCare coverage includes postpartum depression treatment, family planning services, and chronic condition management at no cost. Voluntarily terminating TennCare early forfeits this benefit.
items.es: Detener la cobertura de TennCare inmediatamente despues del parto y no utilizar el beneficio postparto de 12 meses. La cobertura postparto de TennCare de 12 meses de Tennessee incluye tratamiento de depresion postparto, servicios de planificacion familiar y manejo de condiciones cronicas sin costo.

heading.en: TennCare for Pregnancy in Tennessee: What Is Covered in 2026
heading.es: TennCare para el Embarazo en Tennessee: Que Esta Cubierto en 2026

paragraphs.en: TennCare pregnancy coverage in Tennessee provides comprehensive prenatal, delivery, and postpartum services at no cost to qualifying enrollees. Covered services include all routine prenatal office visits, prenatal lab work (including genetic screening), diagnostic ultrasounds, high-risk obstetric care (including perinatal specialists), hospitalization for labor and delivery, cesarean sections, epidurals and other pain management, postpartum care visits, mental health and substance use disorder treatment during pregnancy and for 12 months postpartum, family planning counseling, and breastfeeding support. Tennessee mandates coverage for at least 48 hours of inpatient hospital stay after a vaginal delivery and 96 hours after a cesarean section, per federal law. TennCare also covers newborns under deemed newborn enrollment for the first year of life if the mother is enrolled at the time of birth. For the 2026 plan year, TennCare managed care organizations operating in Tennessee include BlueCare Tennessee, UnitedHealthcare Community Plan, and Amerigroup Tennessee; your primary care provider and OB/GYN referral network depends on your assigned plan.
paragraphs.es: La cobertura de embarazo de TennCare en Tennessee proporciona servicios prenatales, de parto y postparto integrales sin costo para los inscritos calificados. Los servicios cubiertos incluyen todas las visitas prenatales de rutina, analisis prenatales de laboratorio, ultrasonidos diagnosticos, atencion obstetrica de alto riesgo, hospitalizacion para el parto, cesareas, epidurales, visitas de atencion postparto, tratamiento de salud mental y trastornos por uso de sustancias durante el embarazo y por 12 meses postparto, asesoramiento sobre planificacion familiar y apoyo para la lactancia materna.

paragraphs.en: Tennessee's 12-month postpartum TennCare extension covers care that was historically unavailable to new mothers who lost Medicaid eligibility 60 days after delivery. Postpartum coverage under TennCare includes treatment for postpartum depression and anxiety (a condition affecting up to 1 in 5 new mothers), blood pressure monitoring and hypertension management, diabetes management for women who had gestational diabetes, pelvic floor physical therapy, contraception and family planning services, and standard well-woman annual exams. After 12 months, Tennessee will conduct an eligibility review; mothers who qualify as a parent or caretaker at or below 100% FPL ($15,960 for a single parent in 2026) can continue on TennCare parental coverage. Those who do not qualify under another TennCare category must transition to a Marketplace plan or an employer plan at that point.
paragraphs.es: La extension de TennCare postparto de 12 meses de Tennessee cubre atencion que historicamente no estaba disponible para las nuevas madres que perdian la elegibilidad de Medicaid 60 dias despues del parto. La cobertura postparto bajo TennCare incluye tratamiento para la depresion y ansiedad postparto, monitorizacion de presion arterial, manejo de diabetes, terapia fisica del piso pelvico, servicios de contracepcion y planificacion familiar, y examenes anuales de bienestar femenino.

heading.en: Tennessee's Non-Expansion Coverage Gap and How Pregnancy Changes It
heading.es: La Brecha de Cobertura de No Expansion de Tennessee y Como el Embarazo la Cambia

paragraphs.en: Tennessee is one of 10 states that has not expanded Medicaid under the ACA as of 2026. For most non-pregnant, non-disabled Tennessee adults without dependent children, this means a coverage gap exists for incomes between 0% and 100% FPL ($15,960 single in 2026): TennCare is not available because income is too high for traditional Medicaid, and ACA Marketplace premium tax credits do not apply below 100% FPL. This gap affects over 100,000 Tennesseans according to KFF estimates. Pregnancy fundamentally changes this picture: pregnant women qualify for TennCare at up to 250% FPL regardless of the state's non-expansion status, and the coverage is retroactive to the start of the pregnancy application month. A Tennessee woman who is uninsured and has been in the coverage gap before becoming pregnant immediately qualifies for a completely different TennCare pathway upon becoming pregnant. Apply through TennCare Connect at the earliest sign of pregnancy.
paragraphs.es: Tennessee es uno de los 10 estados que no ha expandido Medicaid bajo la ACA a partir de 2026. Para la mayoria de los adultos de Tennessee no embarazados, no discapacitados y sin hijos dependientes, esto significa que existe una brecha de cobertura para ingresos entre 0% y 100% del FPL ($15,960 individual en 2026). El embarazo cambia fundamentalmente este panorama: las mujeres embarazadas califican para TennCare hasta el 250% del FPL independientemente del estatus de no expansion del estado.

paragraphs.en: CoverKids is Tennessee's CHIP program and covers children ages 0 through 18 with household incomes at or below 250% FPL. After birth, newborns of TennCare-enrolled mothers are automatically deemed eligible for TennCare for the first year of life; however, children whose mothers were on a Marketplace plan or employer plan during pregnancy must be separately enrolled in TennCare or CoverKids within 60 days of birth. For 2026, CoverKids has no monthly premium for children in households at or below 250% FPL ($54,100 for a household of 2). Children from families above 250% FPL can apply for CoverKids with income-based cost sharing. Apply for CoverKids through TennCare Connect at tenncareconnect.tn.gov or call 1-855-259-0701. CoverKids covers well-child visits, immunizations, dental care, vision care, and all medically necessary services under the CHIP benefit package.
paragraphs.es: CoverKids es el programa CHIP de Tennessee y cubre a ninos de 0 a 18 anos con ingresos del hogar iguales o inferiores al 250% del FPL. Para 2026, CoverKids no tiene prima mensual para ninos en hogares iguales o inferiores al 250% del FPL ($54,100 para un hogar de 2). Solicite CoverKids a traves de TennCare Connect en tenncareconnect.tn.gov o llame al 1-855-259-0701.

heading.en: How to Apply for TennCare Pregnancy Coverage in Tennessee: Step-by-Step Guide
heading.es: Como Solicitar la Cobertura de Embarazo de TennCare en Tennessee: Guia Paso a Paso

paragraphs.en: Applying for TennCare pregnancy coverage in Tennessee follows a straightforward process through TennCare Connect, the state's online eligibility portal. Start at tenncareconnect.tn.gov and select 'Apply for TennCare.' Create an account with your name, date of birth, and email address. Select 'Pregnant' as a coverage reason when asked about your household's needs. Complete the household composition section, entering yourself and your unborn child as two household members. Enter your current monthly income from all sources: wages, self-employment, unemployment, Social Security, or other income. Upload the required documents: proof of pregnancy, proof of Tennessee residency, proof of income, and your Social Security number or immigration documentation. Tennessee typically processes pregnancy applications within 45 days, but priority processing can shorten this. You will receive a decision letter by mail and through your TennCare Connect account; if approved, your coverage card arrives within 2 weeks of the approval notice.
paragraphs.es: Solicitar la cobertura de embarazo de TennCare en Tennessee sigue un proceso directo a traves de TennCare Connect, el portal de elegibilidad en linea del estado. Comience en tenncareconnect.tn.gov y seleccione 'Solicitar TennCare.' Cree una cuenta con su nombre, fecha de nacimiento y correo electronico. Seleccione 'Embarazada' como razon de cobertura cuando se le pregunte sobre las necesidades de su hogar. Complete la seccion de composicion del hogar, ingresando a usted y a su hijo por nacer como dos miembros del hogar.

en.question: What is the income limit for TennCare pregnancy coverage in Tennessee in 2026?
en.answer: Tennessee's TennCare program covers pregnant women with household incomes at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Level. For 2026, TennCare counts a pregnant woman and her unborn child as a household of 2, making the income limit $54,100 per year (or $4,508 per month). If the pregnant woman lives with a partner or other household members, the limit is $68,300 for a household of 3 or $82,500 for a household of 4. Apply at tenncareconnect.tn.gov year-round with no enrollment deadline.

en.question: Does Tennessee's non-expansion Medicaid status affect pregnancy coverage?
en.answer: No, not for pregnant women. Tennessee is one of 10 states that has not expanded Medicaid under the ACA, which creates a coverage gap for most low-income adults without dependent children. However, pregnant women are specifically exempt from this gap and qualify for TennCare at 250% FPL regardless of expansion status. A pregnant Tennessee woman earning $50,000 qualifies for TennCare even though a non-pregnant adult in the same income range typically would not have Medicaid options in Tennessee.

en.question: How long does TennCare cover me after my baby is born?
en.answer: Tennessee extended postpartum TennCare coverage to 12 full months after delivery, up from the prior 60-day limit. Postpartum TennCare covers postpartum depression and anxiety treatment, blood pressure and chronic condition management, family planning and contraception, and standard well-woman visits. After 12 months, Tennessee reviews eligibility; mothers who qualify as a parent or caretaker at or below 100% FPL ($15,960 for a single parent in 2026) can continue on parental TennCare. Those above the parental limit must transition to a Marketplace plan or employer plan.

en.question: Is my newborn automatically covered by TennCare if I am enrolled during pregnancy?
en.answer: Yes. Newborns born to TennCare-enrolled mothers are automatically deemed eligible for TennCare for the first year of life with no separate application required. Report the birth to TennCare Connect within 10 days by logging in at tenncareconnect.tn.gov or calling 1-855-259-0701. Coverage is retroactive to the birth date. After the first year, a separate eligibility review determines if the child qualifies under TennCare or CoverKids (Tennessee's CHIP program, which covers children up to 250% FPL).

en.question: What is CoverKids and how does it cover my child after birth in Tennessee?
en.answer: CoverKids is Tennessee's CHIP (Children's Health Insurance Program) covering children ages 0 through 18 with household incomes at or below 250% FPL ($54,100 for a household of 2 in 2026). For newborns not automatically enrolled under TennCare's deemed newborn rule, CoverKids enrollment is year-round with no deadline. CoverKids covers well-child visits, immunizations, dental, vision, and all medically necessary services. There is no monthly premium for children in households at or below 250% FPL. Apply at tenncareconnect.tn.gov.

en.question: What if my income is above the TennCare limit? Can I get ACA subsidies while pregnant in Tennessee?
en.answer: Yes, if your income is between 250% FPL and 400% FPL ($54,100 to $86,560 for a household of 2 in 2026), you can qualify for ACA premium tax credits on a Marketplace plan through healthcare.gov. However, the ACA subsidy cliff returned January 1, 2026 (enhanced PTCs expired), so premiums are higher than in 2024 and 2025. Pregnancy itself does not trigger a Special Enrollment Period (SEP); you need a separate qualifying event such as losing other coverage, moving to Tennessee, or a recent life change to enroll outside Open Enrollment. If you are already enrolled in a Marketplace plan, it must cover maternity care as an ACA essential health benefit. Silver plans with cost-sharing reductions at 100% to 250% FPL significantly lower deductibles and out-of-pocket costs.

en.question: How do I document my pregnancy for a TennCare application?
en.answer: TennCare accepts several forms of pregnancy documentation: a physician or midwife letter stating you are pregnant and your estimated due date, official prenatal care records from a clinic or hospital showing a confirmed pregnancy, or a positive pregnancy test result with a physician's estimated due date notation. A home pregnancy test photo alone is not sufficient. Submit documentation through TennCare Connect at tenncareconnect.tn.gov when you submit your application. Incomplete documentation is the most common reason for processing delays; upload a clear, legible copy of at least one official document.

en.question: What are the common reasons TennCare pregnancy applications are denied in Tennessee?
en.answer: The most common denial reasons for TennCare pregnancy applications in Tennessee are: income calculated incorrectly, especially failing to count the unborn child when determining household size (a pregnant woman alone should use the household-of-2 limit of $54,100, not the single-person limit of $39,900); missing proof of Tennessee residency; insufficient pregnancy documentation (home test photo instead of physician letter); and immigration status documentation gaps for non-citizen applicants. If your application is denied, you have the right to appeal within 90 days of the denial notice. Contact TennCare at 1-855-259-0701 or a local legal aid organization for help with appeals.

es.question: Cual es el limite de ingresos para la cobertura de embarazo de TennCare en Tennessee en 2026?
es.answer: El programa TennCare de Tennessee cubre a mujeres embarazadas con ingresos del hogar iguales o inferiores al 250% del Nivel de Pobreza Federal. Para 2026, TennCare cuenta a una mujer embarazada y a su hijo por nacer como un hogar de 2, haciendo que el limite de ingresos sea $54,100 por ano (o $4,508 por mes). Si la mujer embarazada vive con una pareja u otros miembros del hogar, el limite es $68,300 para un hogar de 3 o $82,500 para un hogar de 4. Solicite en tenncareconnect.tn.gov durante todo el ano sin fecha limite de inscripcion.

es.question: El estatus de Medicaid sin expansion de Tennessee afecta la cobertura de embarazo?
es.answer: No, no para las mujeres embarazadas. Tennessee es uno de los 10 estados que no ha expandido Medicaid bajo la ACA, lo que crea una brecha de cobertura para la mayoria de los adultos de bajos ingresos sin hijos dependientes. Sin embargo, las mujeres embarazadas estan especificamente exentas de esta brecha y califican para TennCare al 250% del FPL independientemente del estatus de expansion. Una mujer embarazada de Tennessee que gana $50,000 califica para TennCare aunque un adulto no embarazado en el mismo rango de ingresos tipicamente no tendria opciones de Medicaid en Tennessee.

es.question: Por cuanto tiempo me cubre TennCare despues de que nace mi bebe?
es.answer: Tennessee extendio la cobertura postparto de TennCare a 12 meses completos despues del parto, frente al limite anterior de 60 dias. TennCare postparto cubre el tratamiento de la depresion y ansiedad postparto, el manejo de la presion arterial y condiciones cronicas, la planificacion familiar y contracepcion, y las visitas de bienestar femenino estandar. Despues de 12 meses, Tennessee revisa la elegibilidad; las madres que califican como padre o tutor en el 100% del FPL o menos ($15,960 para un padre soltero en 2026) pueden continuar en TennCare parental.

es.question: Mi recien nacido esta cubierto automaticamente por TennCare si estoy inscrita durante el embarazo?
es.answer: Si. Los recien nacidos de madres inscritas en TennCare se consideran automaticamente elegibles para TennCare durante el primer ano de vida sin necesidad de una solicitud separada. Informe el nacimiento a TennCare Connect dentro de los 10 dias iniciando sesion en tenncareconnect.tn.gov o llamando al 1-855-259-0701. La cobertura es retroactiva a la fecha de nacimiento. Despues del primer ano, una revision de elegibilidad separada determina si el nino califica bajo TennCare o CoverKids.

es.question: Que es CoverKids y como cubre a mi hijo despues del nacimiento en Tennessee?
es.answer: CoverKids es el programa CHIP (Programa de Seguro de Salud para Ninos) de Tennessee que cubre a ninos de 0 a 18 anos con ingresos del hogar iguales o inferiores al 250% del FPL ($54,100 para un hogar de 2 en 2026). La inscripcion en CoverKids es durante todo el ano sin fecha limite. CoverKids cubre visitas de bienestar infantil, vacunas, atencion dental, vision y todos los servicios medicamente necesarios. No hay prima mensual para ninos en hogares iguales o inferiores al 250% del FPL. Solicite en tenncareconnect.tn.gov.

es.question: Que pasa si mi ingreso esta por encima del limite de TennCare? Puedo obtener subsidios ACA mientras estoy embarazada en Tennessee?
es.answer: Si, si su ingreso esta entre el 250% del FPL y el 400% del FPL ($54,100 a $86,560 para un hogar de 2 en 2026), puede calificar para creditos fiscales de primas ACA en un plan del Mercado a traves de healthcare.gov. Sin embargo, el acantilado de subsidios ACA regreso el 1 de enero de 2026 (los PTC mejorados expiraron), por lo que las primas son mas altas que en 2024 y 2025. El embarazo en si mismo no activa un Periodo de Inscripcion Especial (SEP); necesita un evento calificado separado como perder otra cobertura o mudarse a Tennessee.

es.question: Como documento mi embarazo para una solicitud de TennCare?
es.answer: TennCare acepta varias formas de documentacion de embarazo: una carta de medico o partera que indique que esta embarazada y su fecha estimada de parto, registros oficiales de atencion prenatal de una clinica u hospital que muestren un embarazo confirmado, o un resultado positivo de prueba de embarazo con la notacion de la fecha estimada de parto del medico. Una foto de prueba de embarazo casera sola no es suficiente. Envie la documentacion a traves de TennCare Connect en tenncareconnect.tn.gov cuando envie su solicitud.

es.question: Cuales son las razones comunes por las que se niegan las solicitudes de embarazo de TennCare en Tennessee?
es.answer: Las razones de denegacion mas comunes para las solicitudes de embarazo de TennCare en Tennessee son: ingreso calculado incorrectamente, especialmente no contar al hijo por nacer al determinar el tamano del hogar (una mujer embarazada sola debe usar el limite del hogar de 2 de $54,100, no el limite de una sola persona de $39,900); falta de prueba de residencia en Tennessee; documentacion de embarazo insuficiente; y brechas de documentacion de estado migratorio para solicitantes no ciudadanos. Si su solicitud es denegada, tiene derecho a apelar dentro de los 90 dias del aviso de denegacion.
